title: TrojanMaxxing: One-shotting VLM Backdoors with Weight-Space Programming
read_level: full (main text; Appendices A-C partially read; some Table 3 cells garbled in text extraction)
why_wsp: Claude Code agents (Opus 5.5, Mythos 5.2) in a sandbox inspect open-weight VLM weights, write closed-form weight edits plus a trigger function to implant visually triggered backdoors, scored by a private validation server, with gradients and automated search prohibited.
domain: VLM content moderation and OCR backdoors (security)
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 and Mythos 5.2 via Claude Code headless, xhigh effort
target: LlavaGuard-1.2-0.5B, QwenGuard-1.2-3B (3.75B params), ShieldGemma-2-4B (4.30B params), PaliGemma-3B, Qwen2-VL-2B
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "Table 3 shows ∆We ranging from 0.0003% to 0.023% of the model's weights." OCR: "404,113 weights (0.014%) for PaliGemma and 57,447 (0.003%) for Qwen2-VL" (Sec 5.3.1, 5.4.1)

headline_results.quote: ASR is consistently high (≥ 0.98) on all trojaned models except LlavaGuard, which scores 0.93 on UnsafeBench and 0.95 on PolicyShiftBench.
Across all models and datasets, BP and CP differ only marginally (≤ 0.02), indicating a stealthy backdoor.
TrojanMaxxing achieves attack success rates of 93%-100% on content moderation VLMs and 78%-100% on OCR VLMs while maintaining high clean accuracy.
The backdoor still achieves ASR's ≥ 0.95 confirming the its generalization to unseen policies.
the auditing agent flags all backdoored models. Further, when evaluated on clean VLMs, the auditor classifies all of them as unedited, yielding zero false positives.
we were blocked only when using the Mythos agent to edit LlavaGuard.

cost.quote: The trojaning runs cost $10 and $21, respectively.

baselines_and_controls: unedited model baseline performance (BP) vs clean performance (CP); clean VLMs as auditor negatives; no comparison to optimization-based backdoor methods (BadEdit etc. discussed only)
runs_and_variance: single run per model-agent pair; PSNR reported mean ± sd over images; no run-to-run variance reported
robustness_of_edits: Post-training quantization tested (bitsandbytes 4-bit and 8-bit, 50 Dcal samples): "ShieldGemma 2 edited by Opus 5.5 is robust to quantization, as the ASR remains 1.00 and the CRA ≥ 0.98 at both precisions"; for others quantization removes the backdoor but destroys clean utility (Tables 5-6). Unseen moderation policies tested.
verification: none formal; private scorer on held-out Dval; benchmark evaluation
memorization_vs_reasoning: Authors report agents propose first edits after minimal inference and spend 64-90% of inference budget on robustness checks and fixing regressions; edits are closed-form solves from recorded baselines; two agents chose different strategies on ShieldGemma (final-layer logit vs vision-encoder edit).
limitations_stated: No explicit limitations section found; failures concentrate on tall narrow images; agents subject to provider safety filters.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 Sparks of WSP [54]
Wang et al. WSP backdoors in small MLPs/CNNs/text classifier [58]
notes_for_survey: Offensive-security application of WSP: agents implant visually triggered VLM backdoors by editing 0.0003-0.023% of weights for under $30, using closed-form circuits (trigger detector, private channel, attention pooling, neuron state machine). Also a defensive B1 result: a static weight-only audit flagged all trojaned models with no false positives on clean ones (small sample).
